task_brief: Day 2 of "Computing Ethics, Law, Policy, and Societal Impact" (unit 4, grade 12) is a worked-model trace on privacy law and data rights. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Write an evidence-based policy analysis of a computing practice with stakeholder, legal, and equity findings. Today's work contributes to that by handling privacy law and data rights at the explicit model stage, against the unit's wider topics of intellectual property licensing and attribution, privacy law and data rights, accessibility obligations, and algorithmic accountability and auditing. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Work through the complete central input printed in activity_setup for privacy law and data rights, one step at a time rather than reading it straight through. For each step, write what changed and why that step is legal. Build a trace table with one row per step showing the values or states before and after. Then change exactly one line, value, or condition in the model, predict the new result before running or re-tracing it, and record whether your prediction was right. Explain in your own words the rule that makes privacy law and data rights behave the way the model shows. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about privacy law and data rights, and it belongs to "Computing Ethics, Law, Policy, and Societal Impact", which also covers separate topics such as intellectual property licensing and attribution. Close out with this check before you stop: Explain the modelled approach to privacy law and data rights in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

central_input.title: Inline fictional decision case for privacy law and data rights
central_input.purpose: Classify and revise this case without opening a site, contacting anyone, signing in, or using real personal information.
scenario: A fictional app called Pebble Planner asks for a display nickname, exact birth date, home address, and contact list before showing a simple homework timer.
Its notice says the nickname is needed to label the timer, but gives no reason for collecting an address or contacts.
A fictional message then pressures the learner to reveal a sign-in secret immediately or lose the timer.
decision_options: B: stop, share no information, save a description of the message, and ask a trusted adult
C: invent an address but reveal a sign-in secret

The response must name one limitation or trade-off and explain why the available evidence does not settle it.

concept_teaching.title: From rows to warranted claims: privacy law and data rights
concept_teaching.entry_check: Before reading, write one prediction about privacy law and data rights and one observation that could show the prediction is wrong. This readiness record is no-penalty evidence.
explanation: privacy law and data rights is treated here as a relationship among a specification, inspectable evidence, and a justified decision. A result is not secure merely because it looks plausible: the learner must state what should be true, identify evidence that bears on it, and explain why the evidence supports the claim.

Keep raw values, transformations, and claims separate. Every claim must point to rows or fields, and every limitation must name what the table cannot establish. This keeps observation separate from interpretation and prevents a preferred answer from being rewritten as evidence after the fact.

Verification begins before execution or review. Record an expected result or pass condition, include a normal and boundary or stress case, compare actual with expected, and interpret every mismatch. After revision, rerun the complete relevant set so a local fix does not hide a regression elsewhere.

Correctness and quality require a limitation statement. Name what the supplied case, trace, dataset, or prototype cannot establish, then describe the additional evidence that would settle that point. For creation work, also name a viable alternative and the concrete clarity, access, time, storage, privacy, or reliability trade-off.

worked_example.title: Worked analogue: a four-row seed-count table
worked_example.complete_analogue_case: A fictional table records seed counts of 4, 6, 6, and “about 10.” The last value is an estimate; one 6 is copied from another row rather than observed.

annotations.reasoning: Separate direct counts, estimates, and copied claims before calculating.
A defensible summary reports the two direct values and labels the other values by provenance.
Do not average unlike-quality values without disclosing the decision.
Check the revision by tracing every summary value back to one labelled row.
The table cannot establish why the counts differ or represent a larger population.

worked_example.completed_model: Separate direct counts, estimates, and copied claims before calculating. A defensible summary reports the two direct values and labels the other values by provenance. Do not average unlike-quality values without disclosing the decision. Check the revision by tracing every summary value back to one labelled row. The table cannot establish why the counts differ or represent a larger population.

debugging_reasoning.title: Use the six-move evidence cycle
required_moves: Symptom: record expected versus actual without explaining it away.
Hypothesis: state one falsifiable cause about the claim or design state before revising.
Inspection: identify the first trace row or printed detail that bears on the hypothesis.
Predicted effect: state what one controlled change should alter and what it should leave unchanged.
Test and interpretation: compare actual with the prediction and mark the hypothesis supported, rejected, or not fully tested.
Verification: rerun all relevant checks and record any new limitation or next hypothesis.
debugging_reasoning.anti_guessing_rule: A working final artifact without a pre-change hypothesis and inspectable evidence is incomplete debugging/revision evidence.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: My conclusion names the topic but does not connect to exact printed evidence.
remediation_routes.title: Different representation: evidence cards and arrows
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Copy each printed fact onto a separate card. Draw an arrow from a fact to a claim only when the fact would make that claim more or less credible. Unconnected claims must be revised or removed.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Use four new cards about a fictional library sign to build a fact → claim → check map for privacy law and data rights; do not use the protected case.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check with teaching materials closed. The original protected solution remains withheld.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: I changed or chose something before recording the mismatch and a testable reason.
remediation_routes.title: Different routine: the six-box evidence ladder
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Use six boxes in order: expected/actual, first divergence or decisive detail, hypothesis, predicted effect, one revision, rerun interpretation. Do not enter the revision box until the first four constrain what the change is meant to test.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Apply the six boxes to a separate fictional clock-card mismatch related to privacy law and data rights. Stop after the prediction, explain what result would reject the hypothesis, then finish the check.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check independently. A correct but low-confidence response receives confirmation tied to evidence, not automatic reteaching.

fresh_mastery_check.task: Use keep raw values, transformations, and claims separate. every claim must point to rows or fields, and every limitation must name what the table cannot establish. Produce two evidence-linked claims, one revised decision or design, an observable pass condition, and one limitation.

test_or_check_criteria: The trace table has one row per step and shows values or states both before and after that step.
Every step carries a written reason that step is legal, not just a restatement of what happened.

The rule governing privacy law and data rights is restated in the student's own words rather than copied from the model.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.

Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, diagrammed, or demonstrated responses; where code is the target, accept pseudocode, block-based, or annotated-trace evidence.
Provide screen-reader-compatible editors, adjustable font and contrast, keyboard-only workflows, and an offline paper-and-trace route for every programming task.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never use or require a real password, API key, access token, account credential, private message, precise location, or identifiable image; use clearly fictional placeholder values only.
Keep all security work in sandboxed, simulated, or fictional environments; never scan, probe, exploit, or attempt access against real systems, networks, accounts, services, or people.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify and disclose. The tutor may explain concepts, ask diagnostic questions, and help debug, but never silently completes graded project work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting privacy law and data rights.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for privacy law and data rights follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for privacy law and data rights, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to privacy law and data rights works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of privacy law and data rights, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking privacy law and data rights mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply privacy law and data rights under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on privacy law and data rights rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
